## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible branchless blend with per-particle hash RNG can approach the streaming ceiling on this particle-simulation workload.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill (N≈963) falls below the smallest measured point (N=4000), so every sample already exceeds L1d. The L2 spill (N≈61680) sits between N=16000 and N=65000. At q=0.01, ns/p stays flat at ~62 from N=4000 through N=16000 (both L2-resident), then slightly *drops* to 57.5 at N=65000 and 55.3 at N=262000 after the L2→DRAM transition—no knee, actually a mild improvement. Cost bumps to 62.7 at N=1000000 then falls to 48.2 at N=4000000. The curve is noisy but shows no spill-induced rise at either transition. Death rate does not reshape the N-curve: q=0.25 lowers the floor at large N (36.5 ns/p at N=4M vs 48.2 for q=0.01), likely because dead particles skip render scatter, but the flat shape persists across all three rates.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 1.87 GB/s at N=4000000, q=0.25—only 7.4% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The absolute maximum of 2.53 GB/s occurs at N=4000, q=0.25 but reflects small-N cache residency, not streaming. Across all N and death rates, bandwidth never exceeds ~10% of ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound: per-particle cost (36–67 ns/p) is dominated by scalar float arithmetic and byte-granular framebuffer writes, not data movement. No transition to bandwidth-bound occurs at any N or death rate.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the particle loop. Only 2 vector-suffixed instructions appear (both `movi.2d` for zero-initialization). Particle position data is loaded with scalar `ldp s4, s5` (pairs of 32-bit floats), and all math is scalar: `fmul`, `fadd`, `fsub`, `fcvtzs`, `fcmp`. The branchless blend manifests as 18 `csel` instructions with `ccmp`/`cmn` guards. The render loop performs byte-granular scatter via `ldrb`/`strb` (12 and 16 occurrences), writing RGB bytes to a framebuffer at `x23`-based addresses with `cmp`/`csel` saturation clamps. No gather (`ld1` with lane index) is present. The scalar float pipeline and byte-store scatter explain why bandwidth stays at ~7% of ceiling: each particle triggers dependent scalar conversions and three byte stores to computed addresses, preventing streaming.

## Verdict
Refuted — achieved bandwidth never exceeds 1.87 GB/s (7.4% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at N=4000000, q=0.25, and the codegen is scalar-only with byte-granular scatter (`ldrb`/`strb`). The Halide-expressible branchless blend compiles to 18 `csel`-mediated scalar float operations with zero data vectorization (2 vector instructions, both `movi.2d` zero-init), so the hypothesis that it approaches the streaming ceiling does not hold in any measured regime.
